source.title: Comparison of Batch Normalization and Weight Normalization Algorithms for the Large-scale Image Classification

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares normalization methods and reports training and test performance, including whether dropout changes the test result. It does not use the claim versions’ original interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that cited prior studies found WN competitive on smaller datasets, but those results are not rows. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected networks, adaptive optimizers, batch size, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own qualitative dropout result for weight-normalized ResNet-50 on ImageNet, a new setting bearing on V6. Its normalization comparisons do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that WN gives better training curves but about six percentage points lower ImageNet top-1 accuracy than BN, which their dropout and increased-weight-decay attempts did not recover. They attribute this to stronger BN regularization and argue that WN's incomplete activation normalization and instability limit its use in deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares normalization algorithms, not arbitrary-label memorization or the interventions and measurements in the listed original versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative test performance differed between the small CIFAR-10 network and ResNet-50 on ImageNet; WN methods performed well on the former, while WN had lower test accuracy than BN on the latter.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 test accuracies were 93% for normalization propagation, 92.5% for TReLU WN, 92% for BN, and 91% for WN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization methods yield different held-out accuracy under their individually selected training configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet, WN achieved higher training accuracy but approximately 67% test accuracy versus 73% for BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight normalization can generalize worse than batch normalization despite better training performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing weight decay did not decrease the reported WN overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested increases in weight decay did not recover BN-level performance for weight-normalized ResNet-50.

record.problems: The dropout and increased-weight-decay outcomes are qualitative, with configurations and numerical results not stated. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors note their BN test accuracy was below He et al. (2016a), likely because of simpler preprocessing and a single central crop.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the no-normalization CIFAR-10 baseline: the text gives no numeric endpoint for it. Figure-only training and test curves are omitted where the text provides no additional numerical values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Comparable convolutional versus fully connected classifiers, local connectivity, and transferred initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.

Dropout effects outside weight-normalized ResNet-50/ImageNet; suitability of the unreported dropout configuration; very small training sets; excessive dropout; and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. The qualitative dropout failure warrants a conditional scope limitation, not a general challenge. The fully connected linear-network divergence experiment does not test V3: it provides no comparable held-out convolutional-versus-fully-connected accuracy result.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance under the same recipe.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures.

The paper tests dropout only with weight normalization in its ImageNet experiment; it does not establish dropout effects across the fully connected and convolutional regimes named in the version, or the small-training-set and excessive-dropout cases.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with weight normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with weight normalization; the authors report better final training accuracy than for BN.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison qualitatively.
rows.check: Higher training accuracy under WN does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ImageNet with batch normalization.
rows.note: Compared with ≈ 67% for WN; the paper attributes a 6% accuracy gap to the comparison.
rows.check: BN weight decay was 0.0001, explicitly the same configuration as WN. The normalization accuracy comparison measures no listed version.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with weight normalization
rows.operation_detail: Dropout was tried to reduce overfitting.
rows.measure: Whether dropout decreased the test-performance gap
rows.baseline: ResNet-50 with weight normalization without dropout
rows.value: The authors state they were unable to decrease overfitting using dropout; numeric result not stated.
rows.note: This is a negative result for dropout in this WN/ImageNet setting; the dropout configuration and numerical outcome are not reported.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report no decrease in overfitting using dropout. Dropout rate, placement, trial-specific training details and held-out results are unreported; the six-percentage-point BN–WN difference is not a measured dropout effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 with weight normalization
rows.operation_detail: Weight decay was increased to try to reduce overfitting.
rows.measure: Whether increased weight decay decreased the test-performance gap
rows.value: The authors state they were unable to decrease overfitting using increased weight decay; numeric result not stated.
rows.note: Explicit negative outcome, outside the claim versions’ named regularization condition for V6.
rows.check: Increasing weight decay alone does not test V6's dropout intervention or its joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

relationships.condition: Weight-normalized ResNet-50 on ImageNet with the authors' unspecified dropout configurations
relationships.reason: R7 reports that dropout did not decrease overfitting. This identifies an unsuccessful regime, but does not contradict V6's conditional claim that suitably configured dropout helps in some regimes.
relationships.display_finding: Dropout reportedly failed to decrease overfitting, but its settings were unspecified. This comparison has not been verified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
